Some basic examples were given in [2, §3.2]: if v = 1, i.e. the fundamental cell is simply one vertex, then the limiting measure is uniform. This covers the continuous quantum walk eitA on Z and the triangular lattice for example. The same property is true for the hexagonal lattice and the infinite ladder, both of which have v = 2. It was also shown that in the cases where I is a 1d strip of width 3, or a cylinder L•C4, then the limiting distribution is not uniform.

This gives a more satisfactory concept of a quantum limiting distribution than in 7] where quantum ergodicity was assessed by the behaviour of eigenvector bases, and it was shown in [7, §4.5] that such a limiting distribution depends on the eigenvector basis. In contrast, here the RHS of (1.6) depends only on the graph. Our main target now is to compute the weights d(p, q) for specific finite graphs GF. Because of point (4) above, the theorems are illustrated only for the Cartesian product, but some hold more generally. For definiteness, the reader can assume To = Z in all these results, which is already interesting. However, nothing changes for any To having a single vertex in its fundamental domain, such as Z' and the triangular lattice. A nice simplification in the family of Cartesian products is that the limiting weight d(p, g) in (1.6) depends only on the finite graph GF, compared to the general case (1.5), where the weight depends on the full Floquet matrix and computations become more daunting.
